stories.title: Samantha Atlas of Ash Staging: 5 Questions
stories.excerpt: Staging can play a critical role in residential real estate. It helps to bring a model unit to life, and it provides potential renters and buyers with a glimpse of what their future home could look like. Successfully staging requires more than a properly positioned couch and some art on the walls. Enter Ash Staging, a luxury staging and model residence design business that has completed thousands of projects — including commercial and hospitality spaces — over the last 15 years, representing over $50 billion in real estate. Samantha Atlas, senior director of projects at Ash Staging, has been with the firm for nine years. She splits her time between Los Angeles and New York City, and helped to launch the company’s West Coast office. Commercial Observer caught up with Atlas in mid-August to discuss her time with Ash Staging and the value of her work in real estate. This interview has been edited for length and clarity. Commercial Observer: What is the mission of Ash Staging? Samantha Atlas: I’ve been with Ash for a little over nine years now, and really seen it grow. I run the L.A. office, and I joined the company at a time of growth. Since I joined, the story has been, “How do we continue to grow and change the narrative of what staging can be?” Generally speaking, for a long time the idea around staging has been neutrality — nothing with a serious point of view. I came to work at Ash because we sort of eschewed that. We want to imbue personality. We want our clients and our potential buyers of these homes to have an emotional response — it’s what drives us. We believe in the power of paint and will really push our clients to invest outside of the staging into the property to get it sold. What we really believe in, and how we position ourselves as a brand, is being a partner alongside our real estate agents, clients and developers. What are some of the projects that Ash has staged? bullets: Ash Staging completes thousands of projects representing $50B+ real estate across 15 years
Staging drives lease/sales velocity and achieves premium pricing in competitive markets
Company operates dual coasts (LA, NYC); expanding service footprint with model expertise
stories.summary: Ash Staging, a luxury model-residence and staging firm with 15 years of market track record, has completed thousands of projects across residential, commercial, and hospitality representing over $50 billion in real estate value. The firm demonstrates the operational scale and cross-market presence required to support high-volume new deliveries. Model unit execution and marketing collateral directly influence lease velocity and achievable rents in competitive markets.
stories.impact: MINIMAL DIRECT IMPACT. Story profiles a service vendor rather than signaling market demand, supply, or capital shifts. Relevant only as a reminder that pre-leasing and marketing execution are critical infrastructure for rapid stabilization in supply-constrained, rent-growth markets (LA, NYC). Developers should factor staging/marketing into lease-up timelines and budgets.

stories.title: Proptech Seed Rounds This Year Are in Full Bloom
stories.excerpt: To the surprise of some, or perhaps many, proptech has reportedly drawn the largest number of $5 million to $10 million seed rounds across industries in 2026. To the surprise of no one, artificial intelligence has a lot to do with those seed rounds. According to a Crunchbase report published July 31, at the top of the scale with $10 million seed rounds are proptech companies such as Breezy, a Los Angeles-based startup offering an AI operating system for residential real estate professionals; Grotto AI, a Manhattan-based IT and Internet firm offering AI-based tools for leasing and renewals; and Hint, a Charlotte, N.C.-based AI‑powered home‑management platform for homeowners. There have been at least 15 proptech seed rounds in the $5 million to $10 million scale so far in 2026, according to Crunchbase, which did not provide an overall number of deals in the category. A Center for Real Estate Technology and Innovation (CRETI) report found 30 deals in the $5 million to $10 million range in the first half of 2026 totaling $207.3 million and representing 4.6 percent of funding across all rounds. Overall proptech venture funding reached $4.53 billion across 231 disclosed funding rounds in the first half of 2026, with a median funding round of $6.75 million. Compared with the prior year, the market was broadly stable. First-half 2026 funding was down 0.6 percent from the first half of 2025 and up 2.6 percent from the first half of 2024, CRETI reported. The total number of seed fundings industry-by-industry is an elusive number. However, according to Seedtable, a global intelligence platform for startups, a typical seed round across industries is $2 million (median), stepping up to $9 million at Series A and $20 million at Series B. Seed is the most common stage by deal count, accounting for 29,708 tracked rounds in 2026. bullets: Proptech raised 15+ seed rounds at $5M–$10M in 2026; $207.3M across 30 deals first half
AI-driven tools for leasing, renewals, operations dominate: Breezy (LA), Grotto (NYC), Hint (Charlotte)
Capital flowing to operational efficiency tech, signaling landlord appetite for productivity gains
stories.summary: Proptech ventures are attracting record seed-round capital in 2026, with at least 15 companies raising $5–$10 million each; 30 deals totaling $207.3 million in H1 2026 alone. AI-powered leasing platforms (Grotto AI, Breezy), renewals automation, and home-management tools are the primary focus. Investors are betting on tech that reduces friction in tenant acquisition, retention, and on-site operations.
stories.impact: CAPITAL AND COST EFFICIENCY SIGNAL. Heavy proptech funding reflects developer and operator confidence in operating-expense reduction and margin expansion. Developers should expect rising adoption of AI leasing tools and management platforms in competitive markets; tech vendors will consolidate around automation of underwriting, lease terms, and collections—reducing labor dependency and improving rent-collection certainty, particularly valuable in slower-leasing or higher-churn markets.

stories.title: How Landlords Are Cutting Their Eviction Costs
stories.excerpt: By Tom DeRose, co-founder and CEO at PandaGuarantee ___________________________________________________________________________________________ Contested evictions in New York City are the most expensive in the world, running $15,000 to $50,000 each. But the single largest piece of that cost is missed rent, and missed rent is preventable. I started PandaGuarantee because the existing guarantor services were either too slow, too expensive or too confusing to applicants. The customer experience, both of the property owner and their tenants, seemed to be an afterthought. The thesis is simple: The rent guarantee process needs to be as efficient and affordable as possible. Applicant approvals in minutes, economical prices, and an easy to use platform that ties it all together. The $21,000 Problem When landlords think about evictions, they think about lawyers’ fees and court filings. That’s real money, but not where most of the damage is. The majority of the cost is rent — the opportunity cost of having an empty apartment or a squatter not paying for months. In a New York nonpayment proceeding, a landlord can easily go six months (or longer) without collecting while the case sits on the court’s docket. At $3,500 a month — roughly the median for a Manhattan one-bedroom — that’s $21,000 in lost income before you’ve paid a single attorney. Cover the missed rent, and you’ve cut the financial damage roughly in half. That’s the math behind rent guarantee insurance, and it’s why I started PandaGuarantee as a fast, easy, economical option for property owners to protect themselves from tenant default. 2019 Changed the Math Before the Housing Stability and Tenant Protection Act (HSTPA), landlords could ask borderline approvable applicants for larger security deposits. bullets: NYC contested evictions cost $15K–$50K; 60–90% driven by missed rent, not legal fees
PandaGuarantee (and analogous services) monetize rent-guarantee efficiency and speed to reduce vacancy risk
Guarantor/surety market expanding due to tenant credit stress and landlord loss-mitigation demand
stories.summary: Contested evictions in New York City cost $15,000–$50,000, with the majority of the loss attributable to extended vacancy and uncollected rent (6+ months in nonpayment proceedings) rather than legal expenses. A growing class of fintech (e.g., PandaGuarantee) is capturing value by streamlining guarantor approvals and rent-guarantee products, targeting the operational inefficiency and credit-risk gap in tenant underwriting.
stories.impact: DEMAND AND RISK SIGNAL IN NYC. The rise of guarantor-tech indicates persistent tenant credit stress and landlord portfolio risk in NYC. Developers building in NYC should budget for longer lease-up timelines, require robust guarantor/surety coverage (or third-party guarantor placement), and model 5–10% credit loss in underwriting. The solution ecosystem expanding around rent collection is a red flag for tenant creditworthiness in high-cost, regulated rental markets.

stories.title: Tavaco Properties Buys DMV Office for $29M
stories.excerpt: Tavaco Properties has added another discounted office property to its growing Greater Washington portfolio. The Los Angeles-based firm paid $28.5 million for a 272,300-square-foot building in Falls Church, Va., Business Journals first reported. Hawaii-based James Campbell Company sold the 14-story property at 3110 Fairview Park Drive after acquiring it for $43.7 million in 2016. Tavaco specializes in acquiring and optimizing underperforming assets, and the deal is its third D.C.-area office acquisition since late last year, totaling nearly $65 million. In March, a Tavaco affiliate paid $8.2 million for the 100,900-square-foot Twinbrook Plaza in Rockville, Md., which is about half the $15.5 million that an MRP Realty affiliate paid in 2016. Tavaco also acquired the eight-story, 275,480-square-foot Ballston Station in Arlington for $28 million in late 2025. The State Teachers Retirement System of Ohio had acquired that property for $58.2 million about 30 years ago. “We view Fairview, Ballston Station and Twinbrook Plaza as long-term additions to Tavaco’s portfolio,” Managing Director Sam Tavakoli told the Business Journals in a statement. He also added that the firm expects continued return-to-office trends to support demand for well-operated buildings. Indeed, U.S. office visits rose 6 percent in the first half of the year, although on-site attendance remained 31 percent below 2019 levels. James Campbell Company, meanwhile, has been reducing its national office exposure and concentrating more heavily on industrial assets. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Tavaco Properties paid $28.5M for 272K SF Falls Church office; sold by James Campbell for $43.7M in 2016
Third DMV-area office acquisition in 12 months (~$65M total); targets underperforming, distressed assets
Office conversion and stabilization play reflects capital chasing discounted, low-occupancy product
stories.summary: Tavaco Properties, a Los Angeles-based value-add investor, acquired a 272,300-square-foot office building in Falls Church, Virginia, for $28.5 million—a 35% haircut from the $43.7 million James Campbell Company paid in 2016. This is Tavaco's third D.C.-area office purchase in 12 months (totaling ~$65 million), including Twinbrook Plaza and Ballston Station. All three deals reflect heavy discounts on mid-sized suburban office assets.
stories.impact: SUPPLY AND CAPITAL SIGNAL—DMV. Persistent office distress and deep-discount pricing in suburban DMV (Falls Church, Rockville, Arlington) indicate weak office leasing fundamentals and potential for residential conversion. If Tavaco and peers are aggressively acquiring at 35–50% discounts, office absorption and renewals remain weak; multifamily developers should monitor whether these conversions will compete for financing and construction labor. The repricing of office creates land-value opportunity if zoning permits residential redevelopment; however, capital locked in office stabilization may tighten debt availability for new MF starts in the region.

stories.title: Taconic, NREA Add Premium Indian Restaurant to Hell’s Kitchen Mixed-Use
stories.excerpt: Taconic Partners and National Real Estate Advisors have signed a lease with Samudhra at The Ellery, a luxury mixed-use residential development at 312 W. 43rd St. in Hell’s Kitchen. The addition of the New Jersey-based premium Indian restaurant and lounge brings a new full-service dining destination to The Ellery. Samudhra will occupy approximately 10,000 square feet along West 43rd Street. The space will include a dedicated dining area, bar and lounge. The new location will mark Samudhra’s first outpost in New York City and second location overall. “Samudhra brings a premium new dining and social experience that will serve both our residents and the broader neighborhood,” George Tsapelas, SVP with Taconic Partners “From the outset, our vision for The Ellery has been to create a dynamic mixed-use destination that contributes to the energy of the area, and Samudhra further strengthens the retail and dining mix we’ve curated at the property.” Taconic and NREA were represented by Lon Rubackin, Michael Kadosh and Bevan Cohen from CBRE. Samudhra was represented by Brad Schwarz from Lee & Associates. The post Taconic, NREA Add Premium Indian Restaurant to Hell’s Kitchen Mixed-Use appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Taconic/NREA sign Samudhra (premium Indian restaurant) at The Ellery, Hell's Kitchen (10K SF retail)
Full-service dining anchor on W. 43rd St. signals strong retail demand and residency confidence

The space includes a dedicated dining area, bar, and lounge. Samudhra's NYC expansion signals confidence in the Hell's Kitchen dining and residential market.

Relevant only as evidence of strong food-service demand and residential confidence in midtown west; supports the thesis that Hell's Kitchen is attracting premium operators. No material signal on rents, supply, or capital availability.

stories.title: For Southern California, Defense Tech Is the Best Real Estate Offense
stories.excerpt: It’s easy to assume Los Angeles’ biggest contribution to the defense industry and any war effort has been the production of movies and films that celebrate the heroism of combat. But, due to persistent geopolitical instability, combat that’s draining crucial weapon stockpiles, and ongoing efforts to adapt the United States military to the modern demands of high-tech warfare, defense spending is skyrocketing. And no place is benefiting from that more than Southern California, especially the South Bay, a grouping of small cities adjacent to Los Angeles, including Torrance, Hawthorne, Long Beach and El Segundo, that have seen their port-adjacent warehouse spaces transformed into hubs of military manufacturing activity. “The growth curve we’re seeing for the South Bay right now is unprecedented,” said Mac Burridge, a managing director at JLL who leads the advanced manufacturing team. “It’s very akin to the Inland Empire during COVID, where there was just a frenzy for space and only a finite amount available.” Historically, the South Bay has been a hotbed of aeronautics and space technology. Many of the largest traditional defense contractors, known as the primes, operate out of Greater L.A., and SpaceX, which held its blockbuster initial public offering earlier this year, was incubated in the small city of El Segundo, a nexus of startups and innovation just south of Los Angeles International Airport. That tech activity has recently gone into overdrive, a mobilization that has become one of the bright spots of the Southern California economy. A record $366 billion was invested last year in California startups, driven by the AI boom. But the defense tech boom might be even more pronounced. Last summer’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act appropriated $153 billion in defense spending on top of record Pentagon budgets, with a proposed $1.5 trillion of spending for next year. bullets: Defense/aerospace manufacturing boom in South Bay (Torrance, Hawthorne, Long Beach, El Segundo)
Geopolitical instability and weapons stockpile depletion driving skyrocketing defense-tech spending
Port-adjacent warehouse space scarce and repricing; demand profile comparable to Inland Empire during COVID
stories.summary: Southern California's South Bay (Torrance, Hawthorne, Long Beach, El Segundo) is experiencing unprecedented growth in defense and advanced manufacturing due to geopolitical instability, weapons stockpile depletion, and modernization of military procurement. Port-adjacent warehouse facilities are being converted and repurposed for military production. JLL's Mac Burridge compares current South Bay tightness to the Inland Empire frenzy during COVID: extreme scarcity and landlord pricing power.
stories.impact: DEMAND SIGNAL—SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA. Major employer expansion (defense manufacturing) is concentrating in the South Bay submarket, driving inbound job growth and industrial-real-estate scarcity. Multifamily developers in Long Beach, Torrance, and Hawthorne should expect population inflow, wage growth, and rental-demand tailwinds. Primary opportunity: identify emerging residential nodes near defense-tech clusters and acquire/entitle land before rents capitalize the migration fully. Secondary constraint: if defense manufacturing absorbs all vacant industrial space and construction labor, cost inflation and labor availability may compress multifamily development feasibility in the South Bay proper; consider broader LA market adjacencies (South Gate, Lynwood, Commerce) for workforce housing.

stories.title: Landmark Properties Delivers 1,261-Bed Student Housing Near USC Campus
stories.excerpt: Landmark Properties has delivered The Standard at Los Angeles, a 429-unit, 1,261-bed student housing community at 3900 South Figueroa St., 0.3 miles from the University of Southern California in Los Angeles. It represents Landmark’s second ground-up development in LA. Rising eight stories, the project was designed by HED, with Landmark Construction, the in-house construction arm of Landmark Properties, serving as general contractor. “We’re excited to open doors at The Standard at Los Angeles and welcome our first residents to our community – just steps from USC’s campus, BMO Stadium and Memorial Coliseum,” said Jason Doornbos, chief development officer at Landmark Properties. “The Standard’s market-leading amenities, design, and luxury unit finishes set a new benchmark for student housing near USC, and this delivery reflects the caliber our team consistently delivers at Landmark.” In 2025, Landmark delivered its first development in the area, The Mark Los Angeles near UCLA, and also acquired Icon Plaza and West 27th Place, which serve students attending USC. bullets: Landmark Properties delivers 429-unit, 1,261-bed student housing (The Standard) 0.3 miles from USC

stories.summary: Landmark Properties has completed The Standard at Los Angeles, a 429-unit, 1,261-bed student housing community at 3900 South Figueroa Street, 0.3 miles from USC's campus. The eight-story, ground-up development was designed by HED and built by Landmark's in-house construction arm. It marks Landmark's second ground-up development in LA; the company also delivered The Mark near UCLA in 2025 and acquired Icon Plaza and West 27th Place for USC students.
stories.impact: SUPPLY SIGNAL—LOS ANGELES (USC SUBMARKET). Landmark's aggressive LA expansion (two ground-ups, two acquisitions in 12 months) indicates confidence in student-housing rents and occupancy near major research universities. However, delivery of 1,261 beds near USC will contribute to supply growth and potential rent moderation in the student segment. Developer implications: student housing remains capital-efficient and lease-stable, but new supply will compress the window for additional beds near USC/UCLA; non-traditional housing (co-living, mixed-income) may offer higher returns than pure-play student product in saturated coastal markets.

stories.title: Inland Completes Equity Raise for St. Paul Opportunity Zone MF Project
stories.excerpt: Inland Real Estate Investment Corporation announced the completion of the approximately $28 million equity raise for Office Conversion Opportunity Zone, LLC, a private real estate investment vehicle structured to qualify as a Qualified Opportunity Fund and sponsored by an affiliate of Inland Investments. The offering has been fully subscribed and is now closed. The fund maintains an approximately 89 percent ownership interest in a 16-story building located at 386 Wabasha Street North in downtown St. Paul, Minnesota. The property is being redeveloped from an underutilized office building into a multifamily residential community featuring 178 apartment units and approximately 2,338 square feet of street-level retail space. The redevelopment is being executed in partnership with Kaeding Development Group LLC as development partner, R.E.C., Inc. d/b/a Ron Clark Construction & Design as general contractor, and Bader Management, Inc. as property manager. If you’re reading about the multifamily industry, you should be in the room with its leaders. Connect Apartments brings together the executives featured in Connect CRE’s coverage for an afternoon of high-level insights and unmatched networking on September 22 at The Biltmore in LA. bullets: Inland Real Estate completed $28M equity raise for St. Paul office-to-residential conversion (Opportunity Zone)
16-story building converted to 178 units + 2.3K SF retail; downtown St. Paul redevelopment
Qualified Opportunity Fund structure; partnership with Kaeding Development and Ron Clark Construction
stories.summary: Inland Real Estate Investment Corporation closed a $28 million equity raise for Office Conversion Opportunity Zone, LLC, a Qualified Opportunity Fund structured to redevelop a 16-story downtown St. Paul office building (386 Wabasha Street North) into 178 apartment units and approximately 2,338 square feet of street-level retail. The fund maintains 89% ownership; Kaeding Development Group and Ron Clark Construction are development and construction partners.
stories.impact: CAPITAL AND SUPPLY SIGNAL—ST. PAUL. Office-to-residential conversion in downtown St. Paul, backed by OZ capital and Inland's equity raise, signals (a) capital willing to fund conversion risk in secondary Midwest markets, (b) persistent office oversupply driving conversion economics, and (c) confidence in downtown residential demand near corporate anchors and transit. For multifamily developers in the Twin Cities: OZ vehicles and conversion plays reduce new-ground-up feasibility in downtown submarkets. However, soft suburban office rents create land-value opportunity; developers should assess whether conversion-ready office buildings in secondary metros offer faster, lower-cost entitlements than greenfield sites.

stories.title: Classical Christian School Acquires Permanent Upper West Side Home
stories.excerpt: Denham Wolf Real Estate Services represented The Geneva School of Manhattan in acquiring a permanent Upper West Side campus, securing a long-term home for the independent Classical Christian school. Approved by the United States Bankruptcy Court in July, the acquisition establishes a long-term home for the school. The six-story, 38,838-square-foot educational facility was acquired for $33.2 million and will provide The Geneva School with a permanent campus to support its continued growth and long-term educational mission. The acquisition also represents an exceptional value, with the purchase price significantly below the cost of developing a comparable educational facility in Manhattan today, according to Denham Wolf. Led by Kate Hrobsky and Christopher D. Turner, Denham Wolf served as strategic real estate advisor throughout the acquisition process, providing search strategy, property identification, financial analysis, due diligence, negotiations, and bankruptcy sale advisory. Denham Wolf worked closely with BKREA’s Tom Brady, Ana Barrie, Ryan Candel, and Bob Knakal, who represented the bankruptcy trustees. The post Classical Christian School Acquires Permanent Upper West Side Home appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Geneva School of Manhattan acquires permanent Upper West Side campus for $33.2M (38.8K SF, six-story)
Bankruptcy-court-approved purchase; below-market price relative to new-construction replacement cost
Independent Classical Christian school establishes long-term institutional anchor on UWS
stories.summary: The Geneva School of Manhattan acquired a permanent Upper West Side campus at $33.2 million for a 38,838-square-foot, six-story educational facility. The acquisition was approved by U.S. Bankruptcy Court in July and represents significant savings compared to new construction costs in Manhattan. Denham Wolf Real Estate Services and BKREA advised on the transaction.
stories.impact: MINIMAL IMPACT ON MULTIFAMILY DEVELOPMENT. Bankruptcy-driven real estate sale of an educational facility; signals soft pricing for distressed buildings in UWS but no direct bearing on residential demand or supply. Relevant only as a data point on alternative-use conversions and institution-anchored real estate value. No material implications for apartment development in Manhattan.
